operations: OWNERSHIP CORRECTION: Goedehoop Colliery is owned by Thungela Operations (Pty) Ltd (Thungela Resources), demerged from Anglo American in June 2021 - it was never a Seriti mine. Underground, fully mechanised bord-and-pillar; product beneficiated on site and railed from a dedicated rapid load-out terminal to Richards Bay Coal Terminal for export. Located at Van Dyksdrift between eMalahleni and Middelburg (Steve Tshwete LM). Goedehoop North reached the end of its economic life in 2025; production replaced by the new Annea Colliery with employees and equipment redeployed. Sale of the Goedehoop North mining area (RLOT, beneficiation plant, surface rights, residue dump, mining rights, ~R41m rehab liability) to GHN Resources (Pty) Ltd / Bisichi PLC for up to R700m announced 1 Dec 2025, subject to s11 consent and Competition approval. Goedehoop South (Kleinfontein) still under environmental audit Dec 2025. Site direct number 013 687 5300.
scale_note: Production 2.6Mt (2025, GEM); reserves 6.6Mt, resources 249.6Mt, LOM 2 years (Thungela site, 2025); GEM estimates ~450 workforce
status_flag: sold - now Thungela Resources (record mis-attributed to Seriti); Goedehoop North sale to GHN Resources/Bisichi PLC pending

operations: Province confirmed as Mpumalanga (Lekwa LM, Gert Sibande District), not Free State. Underground colliery ~30km north of Standerton, one of SA's deepest coal mines (200m), mechanised with 12 continuous-miner sections. Supplies ~4.39Mtpa to Eskom's Tutuka power station under a cost-plus arrangement; resources sufficient to supply Tutuka until 2035. Commissioned 1982; Seriti acquired it from Anglo American in 2018 (Seriti Coal). Owner Seriti Power / Seriti Resources Holdings (91% black-owned: Masimong, Thebe, Zico, CIH, Coalzar; 5% employee and 5% community trusts). Site tel +27 17 749 0613.
scale_note: 4.39Mtpa to Tutuka; 2,693 employees at 31 Mar 2026 (Seriti site); reserves 118Mt (2025, GEM); TRIFR 3.22 (Mar 2025)

operations: Opencast mine on the New Largo reserve adjacent to Eskom's Kusile power station, Emalahleni LM (near Balmoral/Ogies). New Largo Coal (Pty) Ltd acquired the reserves from Anglo American on 1 Aug 2018 with the aim of supplying ~12Mtpa to Kusile over 50 years; the Kusile coal supply agreement had not been concluded (Miningmx) and Seriti's current page says the mine is operating and supplying up to 5Mtpa to domestic and export markets, with plans to lift this to 10Mtpa. First mining 2020 (GEM). SHAREHOLDING CONFLICT between Seriti pages: access.seritiza.com/new-largo-coal says Seriti New Largo 45% / IDC 22.5% / Coalzar 22.5% / employee trust 5% / community trust 5%; a newer Seriti fact page cited in search says Seriti 67.5% / IDC 22.5% / trusts 5%+5% (Coalzar's stake folded into Seriti after Coalzar became an 8% Seriti shareholder). Board chair R van Eeden. Enquiries via Seriti head office +27 11 047 7000.
scale_note: Up to 5Mtpa currently, 10Mtpa planned (Seriti site); GEM: 2.1Mt produced 2023, capacity 6.2Mtpa, workforce 706

operations: Opencast strip mine in the Free State (Metsimaholo LM, Fezile Dabi District), 14km south of Vereeniging on the Sasolburg-Vereeniging coalfield; mines remnant pillars left by 1960s underground workings. Dedicated supplier to Eskom's adjacent Lethabo power station (~15.23Mtpa); resources sufficient to supply Lethabo until 2042. Established 1983; Seriti acquired from Anglo American in 2018. Owner Seriti Power (Seriti Resources Holdings). Site tel +27 16 450 7200; postal Vereeniging 1939.
scale_note: 15.23Mtpa to Lethabo; 2,189 employees at 31 Mar 2025 (Seriti site); reserves 82.29Mt (2025, GEM); GEM workforce 1,308; TRIFR 1.76 (Mar 2025)

operations: Underground, fully mechanised bord-and-pillar mine ~15km south-east of eMalahleni (Emalahleni LM); product railed to RBCT via a rail load-out shared with Khwezela. Owner Thungela Operations (Pty) Ltd (ex-Anglo American, demerged June 2021). Life-of-mine plan completes mineable reserves by 2028; Thungela's 2025 ESG report already plans 'closure of Greenside'. Site direct number 013 690 4911; PO Blackhill 1032. Greenside and Khwezela jointly funded the Clewer health post (Apr 2026).
scale_note: Production 2.3Mt (2025, GEM); reserves 17.2Mt, resources 12.5Mt, LOM 5 years (Thungela site); 720 permanent + 408 contractor employees at end-2018 (SLP 2019-2023)

operations: Opencast mine (two pits, No.4 seam, draglines plus truck-and-shovel) ~90km south of eMalahleni near Bethal, Govan Mbeki LM; no wash plant - crushed/screened coal went by 22km conveyor to the Sasol Synfuels Secunda stockyard under a coal supply agreement. Opened 2005 on the old Syferfontein infrastructure. Owner Thungela Operations (Pty) Ltd. Ceased operations in December 2025 on conclusion of the Sasol CSA and transitioned to care and maintenance (Thungela FY2025 results, 23 Mar 2026); the where-we-operate page still says 'expected to cease in 2026'. Site number 017 620 2700 (may no longer be staffed).
scale_note: 4.19Mt produced 2024 (GEM); 352 permanent + 962 contractor employees (SLP, Dec 2019); reserves 4Mt (2024)

operations: OWNERSHIP CORRECTION: North Block Complex was Exxaro's (not Thungela's) and was sold to Universal Coal in November 2018 (R93m). Today North Block Complex (Pty) Ltd is 51% Ndalamo Resources (Pty) Ltd (operational control) and 49% Universal Coal and Energy Holdings SA, a subsidiary of ASX-listed TerraCom; the Universal management agreement expired Oct 2021 and the NBC board now manages the mine. Opencast truck-and-shovel complex outside Belfast (eMakhazeni LM) comprising the Glisa, Eerstelingsfontein and Paardeplaats sections; current mining in Paardeplaats (developed FY2020), with plans to consolidate Glisa into it. DMS beneficiation plant, crushing/screening plants and a rail siding to RBCT. Supplies Eskom's Arnot power station and the export market.
scale_note: 5.1Mtpa (2025, GEM); 912 employees, JORC resource 79.47Mt, LOM 10+ years (Ndalamo site); reserves 15.7Mt (2024)
status_flag: sold - now North Block Complex (Pty) Ltd (Ndalamo Resources 51% / Universal Coal-TerraCom 49%); never a Thungela asset

operations: Opencast mine ~30km east of Middelburg and 20km north of Eskom's Arnot power station (Steve Tshwete LM). Operated by Mafube Coal Mining (Pty) Ltd as a 50/50 joint operation between Thungela (South Africa Coal Operations) and Exxaro Coal Mpumalanga; formed 2004. Current extraction at the Nooitgedacht pit (No.2 seam) using contractor truck-and-shovel for overburden and owner fleet for coal; Springboklaagte section mined out. Coal conveyed to a 6Mtpa coal handling and preparation plant producing export and middlings products, then 14km overland conveyor to a rail load-out for RBCT; Exxaro says it also supplies Arnot power station. A water-use-licence dispute in 2024 put the Nooitgedacht life-extension in doubt (Business Day). Site direct number 013 246 9400; postal PO Box 3385 Middelburg 1050.
scale_note: 1.8Mt saleable 2025 (GEM); ROM 5Mt, reserves 32Mt proved + 23Mt probable (Exxaro); 330 employees excl. secondees (SLP 2019); Thungela cites 'strong performance at Mafube' in 2025; planned closure 2043

operations: Opencast (open-cut) mine 55km east of Middelburg and 20km south-west of Belfast in eMakhazeni LM, Witbank coalfield south of the N4. Owner Exxaro Coal Mpumalanga (Exxaro Resources). First export coal 2019; billed as Exxaro's first digital, connected mine (digital twin). Produces a primary A-grade export product (6,000 kcal/kg) railed to RBCT as RB1, plus a middling product (21.5 MJ/kg) for the domestic market. Enquiries via Exxaro head office +27 12 307 5000 (Centurion).
scale_note: 2.7Mtpa saleable, ROM 3Mt, LOM 17 years, proved reserves 40Mt (Exxaro site); 3.9Mt produced 2024 (GEM); GEM est. ~427 workforce

operations: OWNERSHIP: Anglo American's SA thermal coal business, including Khwezela, was demerged into Thungela Resources on 4 June 2021; current owner Thungela Operations (Pty) Ltd. Opencast mine ~22km south-west of eMalahleni, formed 2016 by merging the Kleinkopje and Landau collieries. Two operations: Khwezela North (Navigation area, currently mined, dragline plus truck-and-shovel on the No.2 seam, life-extension under way) and Khwezela South (Bokgoni pit on care and maintenance). Two coal handling/processing plants; export via rail load-out shared with Greenside to RBCT, plus domestic sales. Thungela concluded an agreement to sell the Kleinkopje mining right (FY2025 results). Site direct number 013 693 0111.
scale_note: 2Mt produced 2025 (GEM); reserves 23.4Mt, resources 48.4Mt (2024); 551 employees (SLP 2019); planned closure 2029 pending life-extension
status_flag: sold - now Thungela Resources (since June 2021 demerger); active

operations: Complex of surface and underground mines (Tweefontein North/South) near eMalahleni/Ogies in Nkangala District, operated by Glencore Coal South Africa with African Rainbow Minerals as JV partner. The R8bn Tweefontein Optimisation Project (2014) built a new opencast operation and plant ramping to 12.5Mt ROM per year. Energy: Glencore Coal SA signed a 20-year renewable energy trading agreement with Discovery Green (Oct 2025) supplying >290 GWh/year of wheeled wind and solar power from 2027 to the Goedgevonden, Tweefontein and iMpunzi complexes. Glencore SA is one of four coal operations in Mpumalanga; no site telephone published.
scale_note: 8.9Mt produced 2024 (GEM); reserves 134Mt, resources 810Mt (2024); ~750 workforce (GEM); >290 GWh/yr renewable PPA across three complexes from 2027

operations: Owner Arnot OpCo (Pty) Ltd: 50% Arnot InvestCo (Innovators Resources, formed by eight retrenched Exxaro employees, plus a trust for 1,029 former workers) and 50% Wescoal Mining (Salungano Group) via Arnot HoldCo. Exxaro transferred the mine, mining rights and assets at no cost (cession granted May 2019, completed Feb 2020) after Eskom let the previous CSA lapse in Dec 2015. Underground continuous-miner sections with planned opencast pits, in Steve Tshwete LM adjacent to Eskom's Arnot power station (conveyor-linked). Ten-year Eskom coal supply agreement signed Aug 2021 (~2Mtpa); production resumed Feb 2022 but under-delivered. Salungano had the company placed in business rescue in Oct 2022 (BRP Phahlani Mkhombo, Genesis Corporate Solutions); creditors accepted a R435m offer from Ndalamo Resources in Jul/Aug 2023 but it was challenged in court; Salungano fully impaired its investment and is in litigation with Arnot OpCo over R150m of unpaid funding. As of the Feb 2025 parliamentary oversight visit no mining was taking place - the company buys, washes and resells third-party coal; still in business rescue. Arnot is also on Eskom's list of coal-station sites for repowering. The company website arnot-opco.com is offline.
scale_note: 0.5Mt ROM FY2023 (GEM); resource ~190Mt; Eskom CSA ~2Mtpa; ~1,000+ former employees intended beneficiaries

operations: Ikwezi Mining (Pty) Ltd, a subsidiary of Oza Holdings (Midrand, tel +27 10 446 8451; Ikwezi Mining Limited, Bermuda, delisted from the ASX in Dec 2022), operates the Kliprand Colliery and Emoyeni coal beneficiation plant near Dannhauser, Amajuba District, KZN, in the Klip River coalfield - this appears to be the 'Klipriver Coal Operations' of the DMPR record; no entity named 'Ntshovelo Mining Resources' was found in any source. Opencast mining at the Kliprand pit since May 2018 and the adjoining Goedehoep pit since May 2022; further pits (Shepstone Lake) planned. Emoyeni wash plant commissioned Q4 2020 (2Mtpa ROM module, frontend crushing 4Mtpa). Ikwezi Ngagane rail siding near the Ngagane power station, Newcastle, for export. 70% interest in the Newcastle Project (12,182ha mining right granted Feb 2012). Community SLP disputes documented by MACUA (2025). No named site management published.
scale_note: ROM ~94,600 t in Jun 2022 and wash plant ~76,000 t/month (AR FY2022, ~1Mtpa run-rate); GEM records 0.095Mt (2022) and est. ~328 workforce

operations: Somkhele open-pit truck-and-shovel anthracite mine on Ingonyama Trust land under the Mpukunyoni Traditional Authority, ~23km west of Mtubatuba (uMkhanyakude District) on the border of Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Park, 85km north-west of Richards Bay. Operated by Tendele Coal Mining (Pty) Ltd: 80% Petmin (Pty) Ltd (delisted from JSE 2017; Bryanston, tel +27 11 706 1644), 20% Business Venture Investments No.1770 (community and employee trusts, R350m BBBEE deal 2015). Three plants: 550,000 tpa and 650,000 tpa saleable anthracite, 400,000 tpa energy product. ~50% of anthracite exported via Richards Bay to Brazilian pelletising/sintering markets, the rest to SA ferrochrome/ferromanganese producers. Original Area 1/2 pits mined from 2006/07, depleted July 2022 and placed on care and maintenance; after High Court rulings (May 2022, July 2023) mining restarted in the eMalahleni area in May 2024 (blasting Sept 2024) with Ophondweni following (satellite evidence Mar 2025) and Mahujini next; litigation by MCEJO continues. Mining right valid to Oct 2046. Somkhele enquiries craig@petmin.co.za.
scale_note: Capacity >1.2Mtpa anthracite (Petmin); 2024 plan 100,000 t/month ROM rising to 200,000 t/month with Ophondweni; ~1,600 direct and indirect employees at full production (Petmin fact sheet); only 22 permanent workers during 2022-23 care and maintenance
